prompt.description: The prompt text that declares the output contract. Paste the whole prompt or just the output-format block.
prompt.title: Prompt

enforced_fields.description: Field names your CODE actually checks for. This is the comparison that matters: a field the prompt calls REQUIRED and your checker omits will fail silently whenever the model drops it.
enforced_fields.title: Enforced Fields

response_json.description: Optional sample model response (a JSON object) to check against the declared contract.
response_json.title: Response Json

name.description: Field name as declared in the prompt.
name.title: Name

marked_required.description: True if the line carried an explicit REQUIRED marker.
marked_required.title: Marked Required

declared_count_claim.description: Count asserted in prose, e.g. "ALL SIX KEYS ARE REQUIRED".
declared_count_claim.title: Declared Count Claim

count_claim_matches.description: False when the prose count disagrees with the key list.
count_claim_matches.title: Count Claim Matches

declared_but_not_enforced.description: THE SILENT FAILURE: the prompt calls these required, your code does not check them. When the model omits one, nothing retries or logs.
declared_but_not_enforced.title: Declared But Not Enforced

enforced_but_not_declared.description: THE LOUD FAILURE: your code demands these, the prompt never asks for them, so every call pays a retry.
enforced_but_not_declared.title: Enforced But Not Declared

response_missing.description: Declared keys absent from the sample response.
response_missing.title: Response Missing

response_empty.description: Declared keys PRESENT but empty. These pass a naive 'key in response' check and are usually the actual bug.
response_empty.title: Response Empty

response_extra.description: Keys in the response the prompt never declared.
response_extra.title: Response Extra

contract_aligned.description: True when prompt and code agree and no count contradiction exists.
contract_aligned.title: Contract Aligned
